bullets.title: Semis selloff continues into NVDA earnings; 7-day losing streak, tech lagging broader market
bullets.body: NVDA extended its losing streak to 7 consecutive days (longest since 2022), alongside AVGO and MU accounting for ~25% of SPY's negative impact. The S&P closed down 0.25% and Nasdaq down 0.71% Monday, but 8 of 11 sectors rose and 61% of stocks were up on average +1.2%, with Financials +1.3% and Healthcare +7.5% MTD—market is broadening even as mega-cap tech drags. NVDA implied move heading into Wednesday's earnings is at 8-quarter lows; options pricing ~5.3% move.

bullets.title: NVDA earnings Wednesday: broad buy-side consensus for beat and raise; key debates on Rubin/HBM specs and credit risk
bullets.body: Multiple banks expect NVDA to beat July quarter ($94-95B consensus, buyside whispers $3B+ above) and raise October guide ($107-108B), driven by GB300/Rubin momentum and extending lead times of ~1 year. Key risks flagged: NVDA financing $500B AI lending plan via RVS/PORTS-Pike (~$200B credit exposure by CY28), SemiAnalysis flagging a major HBM content downgrade (Rubin Ultra ships 192GB HBM4 8-hi vs 1TB original spec), and Broadcom/NVDA CDS hitting all-time highs daily. Oppenheimer PT $265 (outperform), Jefferies prefers MRVL over NVDA.

bullets.title: Fed hike odds rise to 75% by year-end; Warsh speech Friday, PCE revisions to lower core by ~30bps
bullets.body: Market odds for a Fed rate hike by year-end have jumped to 75%. PCE benchmark revisions due in September are expected to lower Core PCE by ~30bps to ~2.7% vs. Fed's 3.3% projection, raising the hurdle for further tightening even if delayed. Fed Chair Warsh speaks Friday; JPM notes disappointment on NVDA or Warsh could trigger a 3-4% SPX pullback. Richmond Fed's Barkin also speaks Tuesday at 4pm ET.

bullets.title: Rates rotation pressuring semis/software; leadership shifting to Financials, Healthcare, Energy, Staples
bullets.body: UBS and Piper both flag rates-assisted rotation from high-beta momentum names into value/quality sectors. The All-SaaS index has returned -2.2% YTD vs. S&P +12.9%; software stocks saw -1.5% to -2.5% premarket declines (CRM -2.1%, NOW -2.0%, HUBS -2.5%, TEAM -2.3%). Semiconductor/chip equipment sector broadly +2.5% to +5.7% premarket on Tuesday as sentiment improved heading into NVDA earnings.

bullets.title: Iran-US de-escalation partially offsets geopolitical tail risks; oil falls ~2.3-3.5%, Hormuz remains risk
bullets.body: Markets rallied overnight on reports of US-Iran de-escalation (Pakistan mediating; US offered to halt siege/lift sanctions in exchange for Hormuz access); S&P futures +0.4-0.5% and WTI fell to $82-85. However, Roth and ROTH warn unpriced tail risks remain (secondary sanctions, Iranian retaliation, China pushback). A tanker was struck off Oman's coast. US launched 'Operation Economic Outcast' targeting Iran's digital assets, tech, gold, aviation, and shipping. Gold near $4,695/oz (+1%) as debasement trade accelerates.

bullets.title: US-Canada trade war deepens: 50% tariffs on vehicles/parts from Jan 2027; Canada to retaliate Tuesday
bullets.body: Trump threatened 50% tariffs on Canadian autos, trucks, and parts effective January 1, 2027, already imposing 50% on ~$20B of Canadian goods. Canada announced retaliatory tariffs to be unveiled Tuesday at 1pm GMT. UBS estimates the Canada tariff change (25%→50%) represents ~$300M EBIT headwind for GM (~2% of 2027 consensus). Diesel prices near 5-year highs at $5.61/gallon (+60% YTD from Hormuz closure effects.

bullets.title: Treasury buyback controversy: Druckenmiller criticizes Bessent; TGA use limited to ~10% of balance
bullets.body: Druckenmiller publicly criticized Treasury Secretary Bessent's bond buyback program as counterproductive in normally functioning markets. El-Erian noted TGA can fund buybacks using at most ~10% of its balance. Morgan Stanley is hosting a cross-asset webcast on Treasury buyback implications for yields and financials. Without fiscal adjustment, term premium expected to move higher; US debt now exceeds 100% of GDP and debt service costs hit 3.2% of GDP (highest since 1991).

bullets.title: Germany Q2 GDP beats at +1.0% YoY; IFO jumps to 88.8, ending 3+ years of stagnation
bullets.body: Germany Q2 GDP rose 0.3% QoQ and 1.0% YoY, beating 0.9% estimates on both measures, with fiscal deficit widening to ~4% of GDP supporting public investment. August IFO jumped 2.1 points to 88.8 vs. 87.2 estimate, driven by improved current conditions and expectations. However, Germany's 10-year yield hit a 15+ year high, and Q2 government spending grew only 0.1% QoQ vs. 0.9% estimate.

bullets.title: Hot Chips 2026: AI infrastructure shifting from GPU-centric to power-efficient multi-component architecture
bullets.body: Industry consensus from Hot Chips: AI buildout is broadening to emphasize CPUs (now ~60% of host CPU share for AI platforms led by ARM), packaging, memory, and networking alongside GPUs. Power efficiency per watt is replacing raw compute as the primary design constraint. AMD's MI455X features 432GB HBM4 at 23.3 TB/s; NVDA Rubin emphasizes scalable coherency via NVLink 6; Intel unveiled Diamond Rapids (256 cores) and Crescent Island GPU for inference. SK Hynix confirmed hybrid bonding delayed to HBM5 (2029-2030), capping HBM4E at 16-Hi.

bullets.title: WFE forecasts upgraded sharply; DRAM/NAND capex pull-ins accelerating into 2026-2027
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley raised 2026 WFE estimates from $155B to $163B (+39% YoY) and 2027 from $201B to $223B, driven by unprecedented DRAM capacity pull-ins (+$17B, +47% YoY) and Intel's $20B+ spending plans. Advanced packaging supply meets less than half of AI demand with a 15-20% supply gap at TSMC. Amazon is raising hardware prices up to 60% citing memory shortages. Ajinomoto's ABF film lines running at full capacity as of 2Q26.

bullets.title: Broadening market theme: long US equities into Quad 1 September; emphasis on non-mega-cap exposure
bullets.body: Hedgeye flags broadening continues with emphasis on asset class and geographic diversification rather than mega-cap tech concentration. SPX risk range 7601-7825 with bullish trend signal; COMPQ downgraded from Bullish to Neutral. Hedgeye risk signals: AAPL upgraded to Bullish (buy 299, sell 318), NVDA downgraded to Neutral (buy 192, sell 230), META and GOOGL both moved to Bearish. JPM's derivatives strategy recommends layering hedges via put spreads, hybrid equity-rate products, and lookback structures given elevated September/October seasonality risks.

bullets.title: Bitcoin breaks $80K for first time in months on spot ETF inflows; institutional accumulation accelerating
bullets.body: Bitcoin surpassed $80,000 and is tracking its 2nd-best August on record. Spot Bitcoin ETFs pulled ~$1.9B in weekly inflows (strongest since October 2025). Mizuho and others characterize the rally as driven by spot/ETF demand rather than leverage, with coin-denominated open interest at one-month lows. Dalio recommends 10-15% gold + small Bitcoin allocation; Druckenmiller's Duquesne and Tudor Jones building positions.

bullets.title: September PCE benchmark revisions expected to lower core inflation ~30bps; reduces hiking urgency
bullets.body: PCE methodology changes affecting software, portfolio management, and legal services categories will reduce year-over-year Core PCE by ~30bps, bringing it to ~2.7% vs. the Fed's recent 3.3% projection. Core CPI expected to exit 2026 at 2.3%. The revisions publish two weeks after the next Fed meeting, raising the practical hurdle for rate hikes despite elevated market odds.

bullets.title: August payrolls preview: 65K expected vs 55K consensus; unemployment to tick to 4.2%; FOMC path data-dependent
bullets.body: Wolfe Research expects August NFP of 65K (private +75K, government -10K) vs 55K consensus, with unemployment rising to 4.16% (rounded 4.2%) and AHE of 0.35% MoM (vs. 0.2% consensus). September FOMC decision will hinge primarily on PPI (Sept 10) and CPI (Sept 11) prints, not payrolls. BLS benchmark revisions expected to show ~180K upward revision for April 2025-March 2026 period.

bullets.title: European gas prices elevated; Goldman warns €100/MWh shock needed for winter storage refill
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs projects European natural gas prices may need to spike to €100/MWh in December to rebuild winter storage. TTF held above €68/MWh on Monday on winter supply concerns. Spanish PPI surged to +9.2% YoY (+3% MoM) in July. Germany's 10-year yield at highest in 15+ years, consistent with rising European inflation expectations.

bullets.title: Housing market deteriorating: supply surges, demand falls, affordability at worst levels
bullets.body: New listings rose +5.8% YoY (largest weekly move), but purchase applications fell to -1.2% and pending sales to -2.4% (down 5.2pp over four weeks). Price cuts at 20.9% of listings (97th percentile), cancellations 14.6% (91st percentile). 30-year mortgage at 6.65%, with affordability at 36.8% of median income (96th percentile). Zillow's regulatory overhang improving as FTC order preserves rental syndication with Redfin through 2030.

bullets.title: GOOGL morphing into major neocloud supplier with $84-108B TPU revenue opportunity in 2027-2028
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley raises TPU 1P sale estimates to ~$27B/GW (vs. $20B prior) at 30% gross margins, with Alphabet selling 0.3GW in 2H26, 3.2GW in 2027, 4.2GW in 2028. Google Cloud 2027 revenue growth raised to 118% (vs. 106% prior) and EBIT growth to 137% (vs. 105%). Cloud expected to reach ~50% of company-wide EBIT by 2028. Three re-rating catalysts: Gemini 4, Gemini Flash, and broader corpus monetization.

bullets.title: SEC subpoenas banks over Situational Awareness fund trading practices
bullets.body: The SEC launched an investigation into the Situational Awareness fund (Leopold Aschenbrenner) and sent subpoenas to multiple Wall Street banks that provided capital to the fund, focusing on timing of trades. This is breaking news from NYT/multiple sources.

bullets.title: Meta to launch Hatch AI agent platform in coming weeks; consumer monetization push beyond advertising
bullets.body: Meta plans to imminently launch 'Hatch,' the consumer version of its internal OpenClaw AI agent, enabling multi-step autonomous task execution. Next AI model 'Watermelon' targeted for October. Sequoia invested $2.5B in Anthropic as AI opportunity accelerated faster than expected; autonomous workflow software seen as capable of creating trillion-dollar businesses.

bullets.title: AMD gains 30%+ x86 PC CPU market share for first time; 46% of server market
bullets.body: AMD has crossed 30% of the x86 PC CPU market for the first time and holds 46.4% of the server CPU market vs Intel's 53.6%. Raymond James upgraded AMD to Strong Buy with $641 PT (+40% upside). Intel's x86 share has fallen to 1995 levels. SK Hynix confirmed EMIB advanced packaging from Intel for next-gen HBM, a win for Intel amid TSMC CoWoS capacity constraints.
